note: Every page opened on the checked date. No UAE source was found that publishes regularly updated infectious-disease or wastewater surveillance data. Study figures are from the PubMed abstracts.

monitors.name: Infectious disease programmes
monitors.text: Programme pages on infectious disease, seasonal influenza and antimicrobial resistance. We found no public surveillance data.

monitors.name: Open data portal
monitors.text: Open data portal of the Abu Dhabi health regulator. We found no infectious-disease or wastewater dataset on it.

monitors.name: Dubai Health Authority
monitors.text: Health regulator of Dubai. We could not find public surveillance statistics on its site.

monitors.name: Open data and statistics
monitors.text: National health indicators such as maternal and child mortality and vaccination coverage. We found no notifiable-disease or wastewater dataset.

projects.name: Aircraft and municipal wastewater in Dubai
projects.operator: Dubai Police research and development (Albastaki et al., Sci Total Environ 2021)
projects.where: Dubai Airport and 49 areas of Dubai
projects.text: Wastewater from 198 commercial aircraft arriving at Dubai Airport: 13.6% positive for SARS-CoV-2. More than 2,900 municipal samples from 49 areas: 28.6% positive. A published study, not a running data source.

projects.name: PREVENT-DXB: metagenomic surveillance at Dubai International Airport
projects.operator: University of Birmingham Dubai with Mohammed Bin Rashid University (Dubai Health), Dubai Police and others
projects.text: Funded by a Dubai RDI grant of AED 1.5 million: samples from airport surfaces, air and wastewater are sequenced and fed to models that flag microbial and antimicrobial-resistance risks. We found no public data from it yet.

projects.name: Long-term wastewater SARS-CoV-2 surveillance across the UAE
projects.operator: Khalifa University, Ministry of Interior, Abu Dhabi Department of Energy (Wadi et al., Sci Total Environ 2023)
projects.text: 16,858 samples from 453 locations, May 2020 to June 2022. Viral counts in wastewater peaked about one to two weeks before the peaks in clinical cases. Results are in the paper; there is no public dashboard.
